intro: Manuscript C of Muršili II's so-called Second Plague Prayer, addressed to the Storm-god of Ḫatti (CTH 378.2; Singer no. 11), joined from three pieces (KUB 14.10 + ABoT 2.22 + KUB 26.86). A messenger speaks for the king. After twenty years of plague, oracles have traced its cause to his father's breach of the Kuruštamma treaty with Egypt and to a neglected offering to the Mala River (the Euphrates); Muršili confesses his father's sin, asks for further signs, and begs for the plague to end. The colophon calls it one complete tablet.

paras.en: [Storm-god] of Ḫatti, my lord, [and gods], my [lor]ds! Muršili, your servant, has sent me (saying): 'Go and speak thus to the Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, and to the gods, my lords: What is this that you have done? You have let a plague into the land of Ḫatti, and the land of Ḫatti has been very severely oppressed by the plague. People kept dying in the time of my father and in the time of my brother, and since I became priest to the gods, now in my time too they keep dying. This is the twentieth year that people have been dying in the land of Ḫatti, and the plague has not come to an end in the land of Ḫatti at all. I cannot master the agitation of my heart, and I can no longer master the anguish of my body.'

Moreover, when I celebrated the festivals, I attended to all the gods; I did not single out any one temple. Concerning the plague I made pleas to all the gods, and I kept [making vo]ws(?) [to them, (saying)]: '[…] my [lords], hea[r (me)] […] [send] the pla[gue away from the land of Ḫat]ti! Ḫattuša [will preva]il(?).' [Break.] […] of [Ku]rušt[amma], the men of Kurušt[amma] […] the Storm-god of Ḫatti […] and the Storm-god [of Ḫatti …] them […] a treaty wi[th the men of Ḫatti] […] toward (one another?) […] by the Storm-god of [Ḫatti] […]. And the men of Ḫa[tti …] by the St[orm-god of Ḫatti] […] had been […], and [they] ca[me] (and) turn[ed away] first(?) […] the men of Ḫatti […]. My father [sent] troops and char[iotry] […], and the border of Egyp[t …] […]. But the men of Egypt […] came, and [asked my father] outright […]; and [when my father] gave them his son […], they killed him […]. [My father] became enraged […], went, and the land of Eg[ypt …]; and the troops and char[iotry …]. And then too the St[orm-god of Ḫatti …] by (his) verdict […] the chariotry of [Egypt …], and he struck them down […]. [The men] whom they had captured […] they brought back, and […] a plague broke out, and th[ey …].

But when [they] brought the pri[soners] into the land of Ḫatti, […] [into] the land of Ḫatti the pri[soners …]; […] in Ḫatti from th[at (day) on] […] [there has been dy]ing. And […] of [the land of E]gypt be[fore (me)] […]; I inquir[ed] (about it) [through the go]d: '[…] the [ma]tter […] by the St[orm-god of Ḫatti] […] — that [the men of E]gypt and the m[en of Ḫatti] had been put [under oath by the Storm-god] of Ḫatti; that the [Damnašša]ra deities (were) in[side …]; but that the men of Ḫa[tti themselves] transgressed [the wo]rd — and (has) i[t] […] (become a cause of) an[ger] to [the Storm-god] of Ḫatti, my lord?' […] It was confirmed (by oracle).

[…] [of the Mal]a [River] […] the pla[gue] […], and then [too] for me […]. [Break.] If there is [dy]ing in the land of Ḫat[ti], then lo[ok], on that account I am doing (this) for the Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord: I keep prostrating myself to you and [cry out] 'Mercy!'(?). Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, hea[r] me, and let the plague [come to an end] in the land of Ḫatti!

The matter that I have fully investigated by oracle — […] the matters that [were confirmed] concerning the plague — I am resolving(?) them and [making restitu]tion for them. And the matter of the oa[th of the gods] […] which was [confirm]ed concerning the plague: […] the oath of the gods I have offered up(?) to the Storm-god of Ḫa[tti] [and to the gods], my [lords]; […] I have offered up(?) before (them) […] to you, the Storm-god of Ḫa[tti], […] and the offering to them […]. But as for [the offering to the Ma]la [River], which was [confirm]ed for me concerning the pla[gue]: lo[ok], since I am go[ing] […], [Storm-god of Ḫat]ti, my lord, (and) gods, [my lords], allo[w me] [the offering to the Ma]la [River]! Let [me] perfo[rm the offering to the Ma]la [River], [and let me carry it out properly] — I am performing it [for the matt]er of the pla[gue]. […] [p]ity […] […] [let] the pl[ague] in the land of Ḫatti […].

[… of Ḫatti], my lord, (and) gods, [my lords …] it happens […]. My [fa]ther too sin[ned] […]; he transgressed the word of [the Storm-god of Ḫatti], my lord. [But I] did not sin in any way. It happens (thus) […]: the sin [of the father] comes upon his son. The sin of my father has co[me upon me] […]. Look, [I have confessed it] to the Storm-god of [Ḫatti] […] (and) to the gods, my lords: it is so, [we] di[d it]. And […] of [my] father […] I have confessed […], my lord, and t[o the gods …] let the soul [be appeased] ag[ain] […]. [Take] pi[ty] on me […], and [send the plague] away from [the land of Ḫatti] ag[ain] […]. [Break.] […] I keep plea[ding with …], my [lord] […]. [And i]f for this reason some[how] they keep [dy]ing, [then] I will keep [setting] i[t right] […]. The [bread-offerers] of [the gods] and the libation pour[ers who are l]eft — let them not [die] an[y more] […]. If they keep [dy]ing for so[me] other (reason), then let me either see it [in a dre]am, or let it be [established] through an ora[cle], or let a man of god [dec]lare it; or — as I have instructed [a]ll the priests — they shall keep [sleep]ing in purity (concerning it). Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, [keep] me [al]ive! Let the gods, my lords, show forth (their) divine providence! Let someone see it in a dream then, and let the matter for which people keep dying be found! We shall swing(?) from the šarpa- of the copper ZI.KIN.BAR (sense obscure). Storm-god of Ḫatti, my [lo]rd, keep me alive, and let the plague finally come to an end in the land of Ḫatti!
[Colophon:] One tablet, complete. Muršili […] […] [the ple]a concerning the plague […].
